details.name: ESP32S31 Korvo Board voice HA controller
details.description: using the ESP32S31 Korvo board to create a voice controlled dashboard for my home assistant dashboard, so the TRV valves for each room are controllable
details.deviceDataNote: A value that differs per physical device and that the user must supply when flashing — an API key, a token, a server address — goes in the spec's `deviceData`: [{ key, label, description, type?: "data" | "file", required? }] (key: letters, digits and _, at most 15). Never the value itself: the flash page asks the user for it and writes it to the device, and the firmware reads it there. `description` tells the firmware writer what the code does with it. A selected framework's own credentials are already covered (see its `flash` onboarding) — do not repeat them.
details.timezoneNote: If the product does anything by the local time of day (a schedule, a night window, a daily limit, timestamps a person reads), ask where the device will live and record it in the spec as `timezone: { iana: "Europe/Berlin" }` (the IANA zone name). The host fills in `timezone.posix` — the POSIX TZ string the firmware sets with setenv("TZ") (the sntp_time block's `tz`) — and refuses a name that is not a real zone. Never a fixed UTC offset: it is wrong for half the year wherever clocks change.

console.setup: mqtt-setup — guided: asks for Wi-Fi, then the broker URI and its credentials
console.note: Beside Matter or RainMaker, Wi-Fi is onboarded through them: mqtt-wifi does not exist and mqtt-setup asks for the broker only.
